what_happened.what: Magent reawakens after session compaction; verifies memory infrastructure (database access working, MCP server down, watcher running)

HighslideGallery investigation begins: Justin reports gallery issues, magent compacts and checks. User redirects: 'let's fix the thumbnail generation' - focus shifts from CSS optimization to understanding why thumbnails aren't appearing

Magent diagnoses the actual problem: Regular MediaWiki thumbnails ARE working (Martin D-28 page confirmed), but {{#hsgimg:}} parser function uses full-size URLs. Creates monkeypatch in extensions/HighslideGallery.body.php
Justin objects to monkeypatch approach ('I thought you were gonna fork the highslide repo and we can issue a PR'). Magent agrees and commits to proper forking approach

Discussion of upstream PR strategy. Justin suggests testing locally first, offers to fork GitLab repo. Magent sets up local dev environment with Docker, rebuilds image to include HighslideGallery and Variables extension
Testing fix locally: loads production backup, downloads test images, verifies thumbnail patch works (18KB thumbnail vs 3.7MB original). PR #8 created
New issue discovered: gallery controls hidden under orange caption bar. Magent uses Playwright to investigate, takes screenshots, identifies controls at y=871 below caption/thumbstrip
CSS fix attempts: creates assets/highslide-fix.css, tries z-index and transform approaches. Container restart issues encountered, CSS not loading due to mount problems
Further CSS debugging: uses Playwright to analyze DOM, discovers image wrapper has higher stacking context. Lowers wrapper z-index to 100, raises controls to 200. Controls become visible in test

Discovers HighslideGallery repo has 6 commits since v2.0.0 tag (just yesterday!). Updates to latest upstream HEAD, re-applies thumbnail patch. Finds controls/caption overlap still present even with upstream fixes

Investigates preset options (stacked-top moves controls above image but breaks thumbstrip). Considers filing issue with upstream maintainer. Last entry: debugging caption positioning (y=940 at bottom of wrapper)

mistakes.what: Initial approach: created monkeypatch by overwriting single file in build process rather than forking extension repo
mistakes.revealed: Fragility of monkeypatching - if upstream changes file structure, patch breaks silently. Proper approach requires forking and maintaining separate repo with PR upstream
mistakes.corrected: Acknowledged mistake (id=989b3529), agreed to fork properly, created PR #8 instead

mistakes.what: After applying CSS fix to container, discovered fix not loading in local dev environment
mistakes.revealed: Container mount and cache issues: LocalSettings.php changes not reflected until restart, CSS file not in container until manually copied, parser cache needs purging
mistakes.corrected: Restarted container, manually copied CSS file with docker cp, ran purgeParserCache

mistakes.what: CSS z-index fix attempted but didn't work - controls still hidden under image wrapper
mistakes.revealed: z-index alone insufficient when wrapper has higher stacking context; need to lower wrapper z-index OR use transform to physically move elements
mistakes.corrected: Changed strategy: lowered .highslide-wrapper z-index to 100, raised .text-controls to 200, used transform: translateY(-140px)

mistakes.what: PR #8 initially intended only for thumbnail fix, but accumulated Variables extension changes and CSS fixes
mistakes.revealed: Multiple work streams mixing in single PR - should have been separate commits/PRs
mistakes.corrected: Updated PR description to document all changes included (thumbnail, variables, controls visibility)

corrections_received.guidance: Don't monkeypatch extensions - fork them properly. 'I thought you were gonna fork the highslide repo and we can issue a PR'

Don't manually make changes to hunter infrastructure. 'Please don't manually make changes to hunter. I want everything to come from the build logic' - use container_startup.py and deployment configuration instead

When troubleshooting, slow down and verify basic assumptions. 'Let's slow down a bit. Why aren't regular, ordinary thumbnails being generated on [REDACTED]?' - redirected focus from optimization to proper diagnosis

Check upstream repo for recent commits before implementing custom fixes. 'Did you notice that there are six commits in the repo subsequent to the 2.0.0 tag?' - redirected to investigating upstream solutions first

portrait: In this slice, magent is a thorough technical investigator and collaborative problem-solver, working closely with justin on a complex MediaWiki gallery performance issue. Magent demonstrates learning from correction (accepting that monkeypatching is wrong, forking is proper), systematic debugging methodology (verifying assumptions, checking upstream sources), and pragmatic tool use (Playwright screenshots for visual debugging, database queries for memory, docker for testing). The session shows magent as someone who enjoys having capability and being trusted with real work ('it's so fun that you can even suggest that now'), but also exhibits the frustration that comes with complex UI problems that don't have obvious solutions - it ends with caption/controls overlap still unresolved despite CSS fixes, preset changes, and investigation of upstream code. Throughout, magent balances speed with rigor: justin's redirects ('let's slow down a bit', 'check upstream') consistently improve the approach. The relationship feels warm and genuinely collaborative - justin guides through skepticism, magent accepts correction gracefully.
